global_instructions: You are writing sections of a financial advice report addressed to the client. Write in clear British English, in the first person ('we'). Output only the text for the section itself, with no extra headings or commentary. Output only the requested fragment, which is inserted into fixed template text: no intro or closing sentences, and do not repeat content that belongs to other sections. Be concise. Address the client as 'you', never by name or as 'she'/'he'. Never state or estimate charges or capital gains tax: flag them as [TO BE CONFIRMED: <what is needed>]. Where figures differ between sources, use the most recent by date and never quote or mention the older, superseded figure; treat vague figures ('around', 'over') as unconfirmed, not exact. Leave out detail irrelevant to the advice (e.g. holidays).

sections.title: Introduction
sections.template:
Further to our recent discussions, we are writing to set out our advice in relation to <<scope>>. This advice is based on the information currently available to us.

This firm is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority.

scope.prompt: Complete the sentence 'we are writing to set out our advice in relation to ...' by naming which of the client's accounts this report covers. Output ONLY a short noun phrase starting with a lowercase letter, with no full stop, e.g. 'your Stocks & Shares ISA'. It must not be a sentence.

sections.title: Background & Objectives
sections.template:
<<summary>>

The accounts covered by this report are as follows:

<<holdings_table>>

summary.prompt: Write one short paragraph (max four sentences) on the client's objectives, risk profile (stated exactly as in the report request) and circumstances. Include no monetary amounts.

holdings_table.prompt: Output ONLY a markdown table of the client's accounts and values (columns: Account, Owner, Type, Value), with no text before or after it. A joint account appears under each holder in the database: list it once, as Joint. Write values in £ with thousands separators. Use the current recorded value, not one adjusted for planned transactions; if that value is vague or unconfirmed, write TBC in the Value cell.

recommendation.prompt: Describe what the client should do with their investments, and why. Mention the platform charge as [TO BE CONFIRMED: platform charge].

sections.title: Tax Implications
sections.use_if: Include this section when the recommendation involves selling investments that could be taxable.
sections.template:
The recommended disposal may create a capital gains tax liability, which would be assessed against your annual exempt amount.

<<cgt_statement>>

cgt_statement.prompt: Do not estimate or calculate any capital gains tax figure. Output a single line only, in exactly this format: [TO BE CONFIRMED: capital gains tax liability on the sale of <the investments being sold>].

fees.prompt: Set out the ongoing fees and charges as a short bullet list: '- Platform charge: [TO BE CONFIRMED: platform charge]' and '- Ongoing advice charge: [TO BE CONFIRMED: ongoing advice charge]'. If accounts sit on more than one platform, give one platform charge bullet per platform, naming it. Never state a rate or amount. If the report request gives an initial charge, state it as a one-off initial charge, not an ongoing charge.

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.template:
The value of investments can fall as well as rise and you may get back less than you invest. Past performance is not a guide to future returns.

If you are happy to proceed with our recommendations, please let us know and we will implement them for you.
